data.headline: Pure Cycle’s quarterly growth reflected stronger water activity and accelerated Sky Ranch development

claims.text: Pure Cycle reported revenue of $8.2 million for the quarter ended May 31, 2026, up 60% from the prior-year quarter, driven by growth across its land development and water segments.

citation.quote: Total revenue for the three and nine months ended May 31, 2026 grew 60% and 51%, respectively, over the prior-year periods, driven by growth across both our land development and water segments.

claims.text: Pure Cycle’s lot sales revenue increased 19% for the quarter as favorable winter weather advanced Sky Ranch construction and accelerated percentage-of-completion revenue recognition.

citation.quote: Favorable weather conditions allowed us to advance our lot development schedule at Sky Ranch during the winter months, which accelerated revenue recognition on a percentage of completion basis during the three and nine months ended May 31, 2026.

claims.text: Pure Cycle’s net income increased 31% to $2.9 million for the quarter, while EBITDA increased 29% to $4.7 million.

citation.quote: Net income for the three and nine months ended May 31, 2026 and 2025 of $2.9 million and $8.6 million, and $2.3 million and $7.0 million, respectively (a 31% increase for the three months and a 23% increase for the nine months). EBITDA for the three and nine months ended May 31, 2026 and 2025 of $4.7 million and $13.6 million, and $3.6 million and $11.3 million, respectively (a 29% increase for the three months and a 21% increase for the nine months)

claims.text: Pure Cycle’s water deliveries rose to 631 acre-feet from 76 acre-feet, primarily due to increased demand from oil and gas customers.

citation.quote: The increase in water deliveries is primarily due to an increase in demand from our oil and gas customers.

claims.text: Pure Cycle sold 66 water taps compared with 40 in the prior-year quarter; the company says tap-sale timing depends on homebuilder construction and can fluctuate from quarter to quarter.

citation.quote: Water and wastewater taps are sold to homebuilders at the time a building permit is issued and are dependent on when the homebuilder constructs homes; therefore, the timing of tap sales will fluctuate from quarter to quarter.

claims.text: Pure Cycle’s cash balance fell to $8.4 million from $21.9 million, primarily reflecting investment in rental construction, water and wastewater infrastructure, and Sky Ranch public improvements.

citation.quote: The decrease in cash from August 31, 2025 is primarily due to significant investment in single-family rental construction, water and wastewater infrastructure, and advances to the Sky Ranch CAB for public improvements

claims.text: Pure Cycle expects substantial completion of Phase 2D by fiscal 2026 year-end and approximately 159 Phase 2E lots in fiscal 2027, paced to builder absorption.

citation.quote: we expect to substantially complete Phase 2D by the end of fiscal 2026 and collect the related contractual milestone and finished-lot payments with minimal remaining development costs. We have also begun construction activities in Phase 2E, where we expect to complete approximately 159 lots in fiscal 2027, paced to match builder absorption.

claims.text: The durability of Pure Cycle’s higher water deliveries remains unresolved because the company says oil and gas operations are highly variable and depend on oil prices, gas demand, and lease-development timing.

citation.quote: Oil and gas operations are highly variable and dependent on oil prices, demand for gas, and timing of development of other leases in our service areas; however, our current expectation is for continued demand for oil and gas water sales for the remainder of 2026.
